classification.difficultyReason: Recover the radius and slant height from areas, use Pythagoras to obtain an exact perpendicular height, then calculate the volume.

content.prompt: The curved surface area of a cone is $80\pi\text{ cm}^2$ and the area of the circular base is $16\pi\text{ cm}^2$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Calculate the radius of the cone.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Calculate the exact perpendicular height of the cone.

answer.short:
$8\sqrt{6}\text{ cm}$

Find the slant height from the curved surface area, then use Pythagoras’ theorem.
answer.worked:
Let $\ell$ be the slant height and $h$ the perpendicular height.

$$\begin{align*}\pi r\ell&=80\pi\\4\pi\ell&=80\pi\\\ell&=20\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

The perpendicular height, radius and slant height form a right-angled triangle.

$$\begin{align*}h^2&=20^2-4^2\\h^2&=384\\h&=\sqrt{384}\\h&=8\sqrt{6}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Calculate the volume of the cone, correct to the nearest $\text{cm}^3$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}V&=\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2h\\V&=\frac{1}{3}\pi\times4^2\times8\sqrt{6}\\V&=\frac{128\pi\sqrt{6}}{3}\text{ cm}^3\\V&\approx328\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$$

Correct to the nearest $\text{cm}^3$.
